preview: Interview experience for the Amazon WoW SDE Summer Internship 2021 consisting of multiple online rounds and a technical interview covering coding, DSA, and behavioral questions.
content: Amazon WoW Interview Experience For 2022 Summer Internship Gauri Shewale T.Y.BTech CE 2019-2023 gvshewale_b19@ce.vjti.ac.in What is Amazon Wow? Amazon WoW is a networking platform for all women engineering students in India that connects them to Amazon leaders, recruiters, and the broader Amazon community. The platform provides an opportunity to participate in skill building sessions, utilize available resources, converse with alumni on their career experiences, and be acquainted with the culture at Amazon. The objective is to help women students build long-term careers in technology. So, I had applied for the 2 months SDE intern role through Amazon WOW drive 2021. There were a total of 3 online rounds for people who applied for a 2 months internship program and 4-5 rounds for people applying for a 6 months internship program. Round 1 (17th August,2021) (1hr 30mins) It was an online test on Mettl Platform, consisting of 9 sections : 1 Hands on Programming Section : (Coding Question was not same for all) And rest (40-45 MCQs total) section wise (4-5 in each) : Data Structures Algorithms Linux Pseudo Coding Networking Software Testing (2 sections) SQL queries There was no negative marking for the multiple-choice questions. Hands on Programming Question: A company has hired N interns, label from 1 to N. Each intern is given a device which generates a number everyday that will be used as a password for their authentication at the office door every day in the morning. The internship is for 50 days numbered from 0 to 49. Initially, (on the 1st day) the number in the device of kth intern will be equal to (5000^k). From the 2nd day (i.e i=1), a new number will be generated every day in each device in the following way: Day(i) = Day(i-1) + 5000 + i Find the label of an intern from the given password used by him/her. Input Specification: Input1 : N, number of interns Input2 : P, password used Output Specification: Return the label of the intern to whom the given password belongs to. Examples 1) Input: N = 15, P = 15000 Output: 3 // Day 0 2) Input: N = 25, P = 25003 Output: 3 // Day 2 I was able to solve the coding question with all test cases passed and did almost all the MCQs. Got the selection for Round 2 mail on Aug 20, 2021 ( i.e on 3rd day after Round 1 ) Round 2 (25th August,2021) (2hr 25mins) It was an online test conducted on the AMCAT platform. It consisted of 4 sections: (No Switching allowed between on-going sections) Debugging section : (20 mins) It consisted of 7 very easy code snippets which had to be debugged to get the desired output. Coding section : (2 questions) (70 mins) (Coding Questions were not same for all) Q.1 Given an array of integers, and a value m, return the number of distinct elements (should be minimum) after removing m elements from array Example: Arr= [1,2,2,4,4,3] , m=2 Output: 2 Q.2 Engineers at Amazon are interested in knowing which software component moves the fastest by counting the number of lines of codes changed in that component and all the subcomponents in the code base over a month. Component nodes have subcomponent nodes that make up the larger component. We’ve stored the components as a tree where each node represents one component that contains the number of lines changed that month. Software component speed is computed as the average number of lines of code changed for a given component and all its subcomponents. Engineers compute this software component speed for all such components which have one or more subcomponents. Find the component with the highest software component speed. Assume there will be at least one subcomponent in the tree and that there will be no ties. Input: rootComponent ------> which is a node representing the root Component node. Output: Return a ComponentNode that has the highest software component speed. Example: Input: rootComponent: 200 / \ 120 180 / | \ / \ 110 20 30 150 80 Output : 180 node Explanation: 120 = (120+110+20+30)/4 =70 180 = (180+150+80)/3 =136.667 200 = (200+120+180+110+20+30+150+80)/7= 111.25 Workstyle Assessment (20 mins) It was a nice BIG survey wherein Amazon principles should be kept in mind. Logical Reasoning Section (35mins) 25 questions Normal ABC: BDF :: EGH ? Type of Questions .. There were some English comprehension questions too.. I did the debugging and the Logical Reasoning section completely and was able to do the first coding problem with all the test cases passed and the second problem with some test cases passed. After 15 days, I got an email that I have been shortlisted for the interview round. Round 3 (Interview) (18th September,2021) (1hr) Interview was on Amazon Chime and a live code pair link was provided. The interviewer introduced himself and asked me directly to speak about one of my projects. I explained to him briefly using the STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) method and my contribution in the same. Then he gave me two DSA questions to solve. 1) Given an input array of building heights,return an Output array wherein Output_arr[i] = Number of buildings visible on left side from the top of Input_arr[i] Input 100 80 60 70 60 75 85 Output 0 1 1 2 1 4 6 2) He then gave me a code of linked list , and asked some questions regarding the same. Sum of two linked lists - Both variations ( numbers stored in reverse and proper order ) I explained my brute force approach and optimised approach for each with time + space complexities. Then after getting approval, I wrote the code for the optimised approaches and did dry runs. My interviewer was a very nice person and patiently listened to my answer discussion. At the end, he asked me if I had any questions for him, for which I asked him regarding projects that interns get to work on, his experience with the company, etc. PS: I had one more interviewer in the interview round but he didn’t ask me a single question :) So be prepared mentally also, to face more than one interviewer. I was totally not expecting this but luckily got the selection mail 5 days later :D RESOURCES: Geeks for geeks + INTERVIEWBIT. 450dsa.com : Solve all questions if possible, else at least the main ones from each section. OOPs : Object Oriented Programming CheatSheet. DBMS : DBMS RoadMap. SQL : W3Schools. OS : Operating System CheatSheet. CN : Networking Cheatsheet. TIPS: Firstly, do not dive directly into the coding. Solve the problem, optimize the solution, write the code, test the code by dry run, debug the code if errors found, and note time and space complexity. In interviews, start with a brute force approach and then proceed to the optimal solution. DO NOT EVER LIE ON YOUR RESUME. Remember that the interviewer is not your enemy. Think out loud. Always have a look at some interview experiences beforehand. Practice your technical introduction. Each interview teaches you something you need to work on. Don’t forget to research about the company. Prepare for behavioral questions too. Always ask the interviewer something when they ask you whether you have any questions for them. Stay calm and focused during the interviews and the entire process.
